claims.text: Headline: A Nepali schoolteacher drowns as diesel prices hit a record, while the world argues over who should pay for wars
claims.note: Teacher invented; headline joins unrelated stories. Replaced.

claims.text: Subheadline: the price of fuel becomes a death sentence for the same family
claims.note: Rhetorical, no fact; replaced.

claims.text: Asha Karki, 22, a teacher from Barpak, drowned with her 6-year-old son Laxmi on September 4 after lifting a child from a flooded classroom
claims.note: No report found; unnamed private individual with name and village and no source. The 26 Aug floods were on the Bhote Koshi/Trishuli, not in Barpak. Invented.

claims.text: Jim Harlow, a long-haul trucker out of Dallas, whose weekly earnings dropped 12 percent, quoted: 'I'm paying for someone else's war with every mile'
claims.note: Invented person and quote.

claims.text: US diesel hit $5.28 per gallon, a record
claims.note: AP (syndicated on ABC7), 4 Sept: record national average of $5.85 a gallon, beating about $5.82 set in June 2022. Record itself supported; figure wrong.

claims.text: The diesel record was set in the wake of the Iran war
claims.note: AP attributes the rise to the Iran war disrupting fuel flows, with tanker traffic bottlenecked in the Strait of Hormuz. 'Iran-Israel conflict' wording not used by AP.

claims.text: Press TV ran a piece titled 'US diesel prices hit record high as war on Iran backfires'
claims.note: Press TV article not found in two searches.

claims.text: Iran's judiciary chief urged BRICS to prosecute alleged war crimes, Press TV reported
claims.note: Press TV, 5 Sept: Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Ejei at the BRICS Chief Justices' Forum in New Delhi.

claims.text: The call was a challenge to the 'snapback illusion' of the US-E3 resolution
claims.note: No source links the BRICS remarks to snapback.

claims.text: BRICS nations are scrambling for cheaper energy while the West tightens sanctions that push prices into the stratosphere
claims.note: Unsourced analysis.

claims.text: The Defiant reported Revolut launched its EURR stablecoin with Bridge as regulated issuer
claims.note: The Defiant: Revolut starts EURR rollout with Bridge as regulated issuer.

claims.text: The SEC's crypto-custody rewrite is under White House review
claims.note: The Defiant.

claims.text: Bitcoin sentiment 68, market signal 47; Ethereum sentiment 59
claims.note: internal feed metric, not reportable

claims.text: NPR's 'Voters are fed up with data centers' notes bipartisan attempts to tax the industry ahead of the midterms
claims.note: NPR story exists (5 Sept, syndicated on member stations). It reports both parties arguing data centers get too many tax breaks and drive up electricity bills, and more than $45m in ads mentioning data centers (AdImpact). Not 'attempts to tax the industry'.

claims.text: The same NPR report says data centers' electricity is often sourced from fossil fuels driving diesel prices
claims.note: Not in NPR excerpts; diesel link invented.

claims.text: Inside Climate News: Black and Hispanic homeowners pay up to 27 percent more for insurance as extreme weather intensifies
claims.note: Story exists (5 Sept). Citing a Consumer Federation of America report, it says predominantly Hispanic ZIP codes pay 30% more and Black ZIP codes 16% more than white areas nationally. No 27% figure.

claims.text: Barpak had no floodplain maps, no early-warning system and a thatched school
claims.note: Invented.

claims.text: Wired: Marvel's '42 Hours of Homework Before Avengers: Doomsday'
claims.note: Wired piece (republished on dnyuz) says Marvel's official watch list takes about 42 hours. Entertainment item; dropped from copy as not news.

claims.text: Adidas faced boycott calls for featuring an Israeli soldier in a campaign
claims.note: Al Jazeera: campaign for its one-shoe service for amputees featured former Israeli soldier Shalev Biton. Al Jazeera's article is dated 6 Sept, a day after the edition; earlier coverage (The New Arab, 4 Sept) seen only via a repost, so copy attributes to Al Jazeera.

claims.text: Adidas sales climbed 4 percent the same day
claims.note: No source; invented.

claims.text: Conflict & Security sentiment 48, AI 64, Crypto 66, global mood 60/100
claims.note: internal feed metric, not reportable

claims.text: The UK chancellor will address the economic fallout from the war on Iran tomorrow
claims.note: No such speech found for 6 Sept.

claims.text: The UN will convene a special session on climate-linked displacement on September 12
claims.note: No source; invented date.

edits.headline: US diesel price hits record $5.85 a gallon
edits.subheadline: The national average passed the June 2022 record after the Iran war disrupted fuel supplies, the Associated Press reported.
editorialBody: The average US price of diesel reached a record $5.85 a gallon on 4 September, the Associated Press reported. The previous record, about $5.82, was set in June 2022. The AP said the Iran war had disrupted fuel supplies, with tanker traffic held up in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran's judiciary chief, Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Ejei, urged BRICS members to prosecute those responsible for what he called war crimes against Iran, Press TV reported. He spoke at a forum of BRICS chief justices in New Delhi.

Revolut began rolling out its EURR euro stablecoin with Bridge as the regulated issuer, The Defiant reported. The Defiant also reported that the SEC's rewrite of its crypto custody rules had entered White House review.

Campaigns and outside groups have spent more than $45 million on ads mentioning data centers in this year's US races, NPR reported. Candidates from both parties argued that the facilities get too many tax breaks and drive up electricity bills.

Homeowners in predominantly Hispanic US ZIP codes pay about 30% more for home insurance than those in white areas, and in Black areas about 16% more, Inside Climate News reported. The figures come from a Consumer Federation of America report.
Adidas faced calls for a boycott over a campaign for its Single Shoe service for amputees that featured a former Israeli soldier, Al Jazeera reported.
